0.0.n: Comes directly before a noun to point out which one.

0.1.n: A borrowed English word written in katakana.

0.2.n: Links the podcast to its purpose.

0.3.n: Names the goal that the rest of the sentence explains.

0.4.n: Marks the purpose as the topic being explained.

0.6.n: Refers informally to all the listeners.

0.7.n: Marks everyone as the people who listen and become sleepy.

0.8.n: 聞く becomes 聞いている for ongoing listening; its connecting form 聞いていて leads into becoming sleepy.

0.9.n: 眠い changes its final い to く before なる to express a change of state.

0.10.n: Follows 眠く to describe a change into a sleepy state.

0.11.n: Turns the preceding description into a noun phrase that identifies the purpose.

1.0.n: A neutral way for the speaker to refer to themself.

1.1.n: Adds the speaker to the listeners mentioned in the previous line.

1.3.n: Refers back to the speaker here; 自分の emphasizes whose podcast it is.

1.4.n: Connects 自分 to ポッドキャスト to show ownership.

1.5.n: Here it refers to the speaker’s own show.

1.6.n: Marks the podcast as what the speaker listens to.

1.7.n: The connecting て-form of 聞く links listening with becoming sleepy.

1.8.n: 眠い takes the く-form before なる to describe entering this state.

1.9.n: Together with 眠く, it describes growing drowsy rather than already being drowsy.

1.10.n: Makes the preceding clause a noun phrase, adding another goal to the previous line.

2.0.n: Addresses the listeners collectively in a friendly, informal way.

2.1.n: Links everyone to the sleep aid, identifying whose aid the podcast would be.

2.2.n: Forms the first part of 睡眠導入剤, a compound usually referring to sleep-inducing medication.

2.3.n: 導入剤 combines with 睡眠 to mean sleep medication, used figuratively here for the podcast.

2.4.n: Marks the role the podcast would take on with なる.

2.5.m: would be good if it became
2.5.n: なれば is the if-form of なる; adding いい expresses a desired outcome.

2.6.n: Adds a gentle, personal wish to なればいい.

2.7.n: Marks the preceding wish as the content of the speaker’s thought.

2.8.n: The polite ongoing form of 思う presents this wish as something the speaker continues to hold.

0.lit: This podcast’s purpose: everyone listening and becoming sleepy.
0.tip: Ending the clause with こと turns becoming sleepy while listening into the purpose being described.

1.lit: Me too: listening to my own podcast and becoming sleepy.
1.tip: This is a continuation: the idea of a purpose carries over from the previous sentence.

2.lit: I am thinking, it would be good if it became everyone’s sleep-inducing agent.
2.tip: なればいいな expresses a gentle hope: it would be nice if something became that way.
